transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, well, I came in because I've started doing things lately that honestly kind of scare me. I'm a systems analyst, and I've always been pretty level-headed, but recently... I don't know. I've been doing things like just walking out in the middle of major software deployments, or getting in my car and driving around late at night with no real plan or destination. It's just very reckless, and it's definitely not how I've ever handled stress before. I just feel like I'm acting out of character.

Beyond these reckless behaviors, have you noticed a persistent change in your mood, such as feeling unusually euphoric, 'on top of the world,' or significantly more irritable than usual for days at a time?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I definitely don't feel euphoric or on top of the world. I mean, I might get a little frustrated sometimes with everything going on, but I wouldn't say I'm significantly more irritable for days at a time, either. It's really just those reckless things I mentioned that have been out of the ordinary for me.
Did these reckless behaviors start shortly after a specific stressful event or significant change in your life?

Yeah, actually, it did. Um, there was a specific event at work. It all started right after this late-night cutover incident we had. That was a little over a year ago... so I guess this has been going on for about 13 months now.
Since this incident happened over a year ago, are you still experiencing these reckless behaviors on a regular basis?

Yes, they are. Um, that's really why I finally decided to make an appointment. I kept hoping it was just a phase and that I would eventually just snap out of it on my own, but it hasn't stopped. I'm still doing those things pretty regularly.
Are these reckless behaviors currently causing you significant problems in your personal life or your ability to function at work?

Yeah, they are. Um, at work, my recent performance review was the first one where I was actually told that I’m missing key handoffs. They said I've been leaving meetings abruptly and kind of... making the rest of the team work around me. And then at home, it's not much better. My husband says it just feels like I’m barely even present anymore.
Since this incident occurred over a year ago, have you experienced any periods of time during these last 13 months where these reckless behaviors stopped completely for more than a few weeks?

No, I haven't. Um, there hasn't really been a break. Maybe a few days here and there where things were a little quieter, but definitely not a few weeks. It's been pretty much constant for the whole thirteen months.
Looking back at your life before that incident at work a year ago, would you say you have always tended to act impulsively or recklessly, or was this behavior completely new for you at that time?

No, this was completely new. Um, I actually came in to see you because I’ve started doing things that genuinely scare me. Like, walking out in the middle of major system deployments, or just... getting in my car and driving around late at night with no plan at all. That is definitely not how I’ve ever handled stress before. I've never been like this.
